newsitem.title: UK: Racal founder to break up firm, quit - paper.
newsitem.headline: Racal founder to break up firm, quit - paper.

text.p: The chairman and founder of Racal Electronics is planning to break up the company in a series of disposals, mergers and management buyouts, the Sunday Telegraph newspaper said.
The paper reported that Sir Ernest Harrisson, 70, was said to be engaged in secret talks about a spectacular exit from the company he built up over three decades.

No one at Racal could be reached for comment, but the paper quoted a source close to Harrison as saying: "People can stop worrying about the succession problem because there won't be one. Racal in the current form will cease to exist."
Inside the company executives are positioning themselves to run various parts of the firm once they are spun off, the report said.
The sale of security group Chubb to Williams Holdings, a recommended 1.3 billion pound offer announced this month, marked a significant turning point for Harrisson, it said.

Analysts and the media greeted the deal favourably and the company's shares have continued to move ahead. Williams's offer represented a 37 percent premium over the closing price of 329.5 pence for Chubb shares on February 11.

The company owns a data products business, telecoms subsidiary RNS, Britain's biggest telecoms operator after British Telecommunications Plc and Mercury. Racal has already confirmed it is selling up to 50 percent of RNS, which the Telegraph said some analysts valued at 400 million stg.

Its core defence, radar and avionics business would be attractive to GEC as it has recently won important contracts in competition with GEC. The business is estimated to be worth at least 250 million stg.

Racal's radio business might command a price of some 100 million stg and the company's health and safety division, which makes air resperators for industrial use, is valued by Salomon Brothers at 160 million stg, the paper said.
Racal's stake in national lottery operator Camelot could be worth 60 million stg.
"No time frame has been fixed for the break up but Harrisson is said to be keen to reduce his commitment to the business by the end of the year," said the paper.

Racal reported a fall in its half year pretax profits to 21.2 million stg in December, down from 30.1 million a year ago, and said full year profits would be hit by a 20 million stg charge. Racal shares closed 4p lower at 287p on Friday.
